headline.purpose: Card section headers, dialog titles, announcement titles.

title.purpose: Card sub-headers, list item labels, chip group labels.

body.purpose: All body copy. Max 70ch line length on prose sections.

label.purpose: Metadata chips, status indicators, navigation sub-labels, caption timestamps.

shadows.name: card-ambient

shadows.name: appbar

shadows.name: modal

motion.name: quick-state

narrative.overview:
KUPA is built around the visual grammar of sports broadcasting: a hierarchy so clear that what matters is legible at a glance. Every screen answers one question first — the upcoming match, the open RSVP, the live roster — then organizes everything else beneath it. The red is not decoration; it is the signal.

The surface is clean light grey (#f5f5f5) — not a warm cream, not a branded neutral, just the neutral ground a clubhouse notice board needs. White cards float above it with soft shadow. The system is compact without being cramped, informative without feeling like a dashboard.

This system explicitly rejects: the grey corporate intranet, the SaaS dashboard template, and the kiddy-club energy. KUPA is for adults who take their sport seriously.
keyCharacteristics: Club red is the primary signal: primary CTA, active state, live badge. Nowhere else.
Cards lift off the grey ground — they are objects, not regions.
Type hierarchy is decisive: one heading per section, one dominant action per card.
Mobile-native pacing — the layout earns its mobile form first.
Community warmth lives in content (team photos, avatars, event names), not in decorative rounding or pastel accents.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Club Red appears on ≤2 elements per screen at any time. Its rarity is what makes it mean 'act here.' Seeing red twice on the same card means one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The No Warm-Neutral Rule
rules.body: The grey palette has zero warm or cool tint. #f5f5f5 is chroma-zero neutral. Do not swap it for beige, cream, sand, or any warm-tinted near-white.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Never use a small all-caps tracked label above every card heading. One status chip or metadata line per card is fine; a structural eyebrow above the heading on every section is the AI scaffold tell.

rules.name: The Letter-Spacing Floor
rules.body: Display and headline letter-spacing at -0.02em to -0.01em. Never below -0.04em — at that point letters touch.

rules.name: The Single Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface uses one shadow role only. No border: 1px solid X plus a wide drop shadow on the same card — pick the shadow.

dos: Use Club Red (#d32f2f) for exactly one primary CTA per screen and for active navigation states.
Cap body prose at max-width: 70ch on description paragraphs.
Use the soft card ambient shadow and white background — cards should feel physically lifted above the grey canvas.
Use textTransform: none on all buttons; sentence-case reads faster.
Use referrerPolicy='no-referrer' on all img tags loading Google photo URLs.
Write prefers-reduced-motion alternatives for every animation — use opacity crossfade as the fallback.
Use a 6px top border in Club Red only on the single dominant card per page.
donts: Don't use Club Red as a background color for large areas, hero sections, or card fills.
Don't use border: 1px solid X and a box-shadow wider than 8px blur on the same element.
Don't use border-radius larger than 16px on cards or content containers.
Don't use warm-tinted neutrals for backgrounds. The palette is chroma-zero neutral grey.
Don't nest MUI Cards — use a Box with padding and a divider instead.
Don't add a structural eyebrow (small tracked all-caps label) above every section heading.
Don't make the interface feel like a generic corporate HR tool, a kids' app, or a SaaS startup dashboard.
Don't use border-left or border-right wider than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards or list items.
